measures.title: Adoption of state firefighter collective bargaining law
measures.summary: The ballot asks whether the City of Abilene should adopt the state law that applies to firefighters and establishes collective bargaining if a majority of the affected employees favor representation by an employees association. The law keeps the prohibition against strikes and lockouts and provides penalties for strikes and lockouts.
measures.yesMeans: The city adopts the state collective bargaining law for its firefighters.
measures.noMeans: The city does not adopt the state collective bargaining law for its firefighters.

measures.title: City Charter Section 145: Collective Bargaining Impasse
measures.summary: The ballot asks whether to add Section 145 to the City Charter. If the City and the International Association of Fire Fighters, Local 1044, reach an impasse in negotiating a collective bargaining agreement, the Association could request arbitration by a three-person board whose ruling would be final, binding and enforceable against both parties. The board could consider pay and conditions in comparable cities, changes in the Abilene-area cost of living, job-related factors, and the revenues available to the city and the impact of a ruling on taxpayers.
measures.yesMeans: Section 145 is added to the City Charter, allowing the firefighters' association to require binding arbitration when bargaining reaches an impasse.
measures.noMeans: Section 145 is not added to the City Charter.
